probe_meta.label: dense-G (controlled retrieval-mechanism swap of Probe G)

response_text:
1. (Currently amended) A proofed frozen dough comprising: (a) a dough mixture of flour, water, and optionally additives, the dough mixture defining a dough matrix; (b) gas bubbles dispersed throughout the dough matrix, wherein at least a portion of the gas bubbles are produced by the spent yeast component during proofing; (c) a spent yeast component comprising unencapsulated yeast that has been spent during proofing to a yeast vitality of less than 25% of its initial vitality; and (d) a preserved yeast component comprising encapsulated yeast or fat-coated yeast that retains a yeast vitality of at least 50% of its initial vitality, wherein the preserved yeast component is capable of producing additional gas during baking.

2. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 1 to about 8 wt.% of the spent yeast component.

3. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component comprises yeast from cream yeast, compressed yeast, semi-dry yeast, frozen yeast, active dry yeast, instant yeast, or a combination thereof.

4. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 3, wherein the yeast has been spent during proofing.

5. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component has a yeast vitality of less than 25% of its initial vitality.

6. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component has a yeast vitality of at least 50% of its initial vitality.

7. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the preserved yeast component.

8. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof.

9. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a volume, and wherein the gas bubbles make up about 30 to about 90 wt.% of the volume of the frozen dough.

10. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a density of about 0.2 to about 0.5 g/cm³.

11. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the gas bubbles comprise gas produced by the spent yeast component during proofing.

12. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the frozen dough is in its final shape and form for baking, and wherein the dough has been proofed prior to freezing such that the spent yeast component has substantially completed its fermentation activity.

13. (Currently amended) A method for making a frozen dough product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough composition, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or fat-coated; (b) proofing the dough for a sufficient time period, wherein during proofing the first yeast is spent to a vitality of less than 25% of its initial vitality and the second yeast is preserved at a vitality of at least 50% of its initial vitality; and (c) freezing the dough after proofing.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 60% of the first yeast is spent during proofing.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 50% of the second yeast is preserved during proofing.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast, the second yeast being encapsulated or fat-coated to protect it during the proofing and freezing steps.

19. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing comprises mixing the water, flour, and first yeast for a first period of time, adding the second yeast and mixing the dough ingredients for a second period of time, wherein the first period of time is longer than the second period of time, such that the first yeast is substantially spent before the second yeast is introduced.

21. (Original) The method of claim 20, wherein the second period of time is from about 1 to about 2 minutes.

22. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising: shaping and cutting the dough to produce a pizza crust prior to proofing; freezing the pizza crust; and applying toppings to the frozen pizza crust.

23. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising refrigerating the dough after freezing.

24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the dough is refrigerated for from about 12 hours to about 7 days.

25. (Currently amended) A method for making a leavened bakery product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or fat-coated; (b) proofing the dough to produce a proofed dough, wherein the first yeast is spent during the proofing to a vitality of less than 25% of its initial vitality and the second yeast is preserved during the proofing at a vitality of at least 50% of its initial vitality; (c) freezing the proofed dough; and (d) baking the dough to produce the leavened bakery product, wherein the second yeast produces additional gas during the baking step.

26. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast, the second yeast being encapsulated or fat-coated to preserve its viability during frozen storage.

27. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof.

28. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough does not comprise chemical leaveners.

29. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough has a first volume before the proofing step, a second volume after the proofing step, and a third volume after the baking step, and wherein the third volume is at least 50% greater than the second volume, the increase in volume during baking being attributable at least in part to gas production by the second yeast.

30. (Original) The method of claim 29, wherein the third volume is greater than the second volume due at least in part to an activity of the second yeast during the baking step.

31. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 20 to about 40 wt.% water and about 50 to about 70 wt.% flour.

32. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

33. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.
